Method of Attack: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attack using a legitimate signed vulnerable kernel driver to disable antivirus, XDR, and EDR software
Drops and loads vulnerable kernel drivers to gain kernel privileges and terminate security software processes
Attack Vector: Requires administrative privileges and user acceptance of UAC prompt to run the tool
Exploitation of vulnerable signed kernel drivers (e.g., Zemana anti-malware driver zamguard64.sys or zam64.sys)
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of vulnerable driver files zamguard64.sys or zam64.sys (randomly renamed) in C:\Windows\System32\
YARA and Sigma detection rules by Florian Roth and Nasreddine Bencherchali
VirusTotal detection of vulnerable driver by a single anti-malware engine
